name: Pfizer
description: Pfizer discovers, makes and sells prescription medicines and vaccines worldwide, mainly through one reportable segment, Biopharma, Pfizer's innovative science-based biopharmaceutical business (the other operating units, PC1 contract manufacturing and Pfizer Ignite, are small). It sells to wholesalers, hospitals, pharmacies and governments; revenue comes from patent-protected brand drugs, with twelve products above $1 billion making up 65% of 2025 revenue and Eliquis alone 13%. COVID products (Comirnaty, Paxlovid) are shrinking, and Pfizer bought obesity developer Metsera on 2025-11-13 to build a new franchise.

businessLines.name: Biopharma (only reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Sells patented prescription medicines and vaccines to wholesalers, hospitals, pharmacies and governments; revenue tracks prescriptions and vaccination demand for a few large brands until patents expire, then generics and biosimilars erode it.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 segment earnings (before unallocated costs such as corporate enabling, amortization of intangibles and significant items)

businessLines.name: Other business activities (PC1, Pfizer Ignite and unallocated)
businessLines.how: Not a revenue business in itself: small revenues from PC1 and the Pfizer Ignite service business (being wound down, decision in 2025); the loss is unallocated corporate costs.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 earnings (loss), includes corporate enabling costs

brands.name: Eliquis
brands.note: Jointly developed and commercialised with Bristol Myers Squibb (per BMS 10-K); Pfizer reports its own figure, BMS reports $14,443M for the same product. See conflicts.

brands.name: Metsera, Inc.
brands.note: Acquired 2025-11-13 for $65.60 per share cash plus a contingent value right of up to $20.65 per share (up to $2.3 billion); $6.9 billion cash paid net of cash acquired; obesity and cardiometabolic pipeline, no revenue.
